thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — p99 latency breach on /v1/infer (us-west-2). p99 ~820ms (SLO 350ms). Multiple streaming stalls observed. auto-escalation to incidents channel. link: https://internal.metrics/reports/1719004321

maya (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing traces + logs now, starting a quick triage. booking a short zoom.

liam (sre): any idea if this is global? my quick look shows spike localized to us-west-2 edge and control-plane configfetch latencies rising at the same time.

neha (platform): seeing configstore backend 503s and auth token-store 504s around 09:12 UTC. configstore cache miss rate jumped. We had a feature-flag rollout at ~09:10 that changed client-side shard keys.

maya (oncall): ok runbook step 1: determine customer impact + throttle/roll back flag. liam, can you paste sample logs for the auth errors?

liam (sre): logs snippet:

```
2024-06-15T09:12:18Z token-store error: conn timeout after 2000ms
2024-06-15T09:12:19Z auth: rate limit exceeded for service=controlplane source=inference-gateway
2024-06-15T09:12:20Z configstore: cache miss, falling back to DB
```

liam (sre): looks like hotpath fallback to DB + auth rate limits causing queuing on critical inference path.

jess (support): support intake: ~12 customers reported streaming stalls in us-west-2. A handful (3) reported dropped streams mid-session. I'll start targeted outreach.

sam (prod-eng): if it's FF rollout causing shard hotness we should pause it. neha can you roll back the FF? also consider enabling configstore read-cache fallback for inference requests.

neha (platform): rolling back flag now (FF:feature/shard-redistribution). patching via control plane: `POST /api/flags/FF-123/rollback` -> returning 202.

maya (oncall): while rollback is in flight, mitigation #2: increase token-store DB pool to reduce timeouts. liam can you bump pool size for token-store?

liam (sre): bumping pool from 30 -> 80 for token-store: `kubectl patch deployment token-store -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"token-store","env":[{"name":"DB_POOL","value":"80"}]}]}}}'` -> applied.

incident-bot: update: flag rollback queued (09:15 UTC), token-store pool update applied (09:16 UTC).

neha (platform): enabling configstore local read cache on inference gateway for us-west-2 (short-term TTL 60s) to reduce control-plane calls. patch deploying.

jess (support): impact numbers: roughly 3% of streaming requests in us-west-2 saw stalls >5s over the last 20m. No data loss reported, but user experience degraded. escalation to account owners for the 3 customers who saw drops.

maya (oncall): tracing shows p95 back to ~260ms after cache + pool changes, p99 still at ~480ms. streaming success improving but we still see tail spikes on long sessions (seq len > 1500).

liam (sre): sampled a slow trace:
```
span1: inference gateway recv 120ms
span2: control-plane configfetch wait 520ms
span3: auth token fetch 180ms (retry 1)
span4: model-run 90ms
```
This matches control-plane + auth queuing as the dominant tail contributors.

neha (platform): RCA hypothesis: FF rollout shifted a subset of traffic to a newly-created config shard which immediately became a hotkey. The cache miss storm caused synchronous DB reads and auth token refreshes, which exposed rate-limits in the auth path. Combined gave a tail-latency spike.

sam (prod-eng): agreed. action items: immediate = add gradual rollout guard for FFs that touch config shard mapping; medium = add circuit-breaker and async configfetch with stale-while-revalidate for inference path; long = better shard balancing + autoscale rules for configstore. I'll own tracking.

jess (support): sending customer note draft, will include that we've mitigated and are investigating RCA.

maya (oncall): handing active monitoring to @liam (daytime oncall). I'll stay on slack for followups. :white_check_mark:

liam (sre): taking over monitoring. will run a small canary of the flag rollback and watch p99 for 30m. pushing a canary validation now.

incident-bot: metrics update (09:42 UTC): p95=240ms, p99=270ms. streaming stall rate down to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated.

maya (oncall): thanks team. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next steps: sam to own postmortem (48h), neha to implement cache-fallback guard, liam to add increased auth rate-limit throttling for configfetch with delta window, jess to finalize customer comms.

sam (prod-eng): noted. postmortem owner = sam. timeline + RCA + follow-up playbook by EOD + 48h action schedule.

jess (support): comms sent to affected accounts, will update thread if customers report regressions.

liam (sre): confirmed stable for 40m. closing active mitigation. leaving thread open for any followups. :eyes:
